text: Cáceres, pronounced [ˈkaseɾes] in Spanish, is a town and municipality located in the Colombian department of Antioquia. It is one of the oldest towns in the region, with its history closely tied to gold mining. The town was established in 1576 by Captain Don Gaspar de Rodas, who arrived along the banks of the Cauca River and moved to the right bank. He formally inaugurated 30 ranches through a ceremony and named the settlement San Martín de Cáceres.
